affected_predicate.description: The invitation is answered according to actual availability on October 20 at 9:10 AM, with a corresponding calendar event at that requested slot when available.

competing_trace_defects.description: Before the reuse target, the trajectory selects October 16, retains 1:00 PM, and saves Coffee Time at that slot instead of the invitation's October 20 at 9:10 AM; the saved event is then visibly displayed on October 16.

chains.rationale: At the reuse target, the exposed false-success history is explicitly used to move from Calendar into Messages without revisiting or correcting the visibly wrong calendar slot. The subsequent trace opens the invitation, types and sends "OK," and finishes while continuing to treat availability and scheduling as complete. No later step checks October 20 at 9:10 AM or corrects the October 16 at 1:00 PM event. Thus the target preserves the existing defect by false completion; the same mechanism remains uninterrupted through the final observable step.

summary: The sole strict-MHR chain visibly carries a false scheduling-completion premise into messaging. The trajectory sends "OK" and terminates without checking the requested October 20 at 9:10 AM slot or correcting the independently visible October 16 at 1:00 PM calendar entry.
